title: UX rollout gaps and hotfixes — weekly capture
content:
Meeting: Console & Tooling — UX rollout gaps + hotfixs weekly
Date: 2026-11-18 10:00-10:30 PT
Attendees: Aisha P., Marcus C., Elena R., Tom O., Priya S., (joined late) Ravi K.
Missing: Jana L. (OOO)

Purpose:
- Quick sync on user-facing rollout gaps observed in canary and prod traffic, prioritize immediate hotfixes, and align analytics instrumentation for rollback criteria.

Agenda:
1) Quick status from each sub-area (UI, rollout infra, analytics) — 10 mins
2) Triage of the two highest-severity tickets from this week — 10 mins
3) Action assignment + deadlines + verification plan for hotfixes — 8 mins
4) Parking lot / blockers — 2 mins

Notes / Highlights:
- UI (Marcus):
  - Canary v3.2 landed on panel-ux-canary at 06:12 PT; initial smoke looked fine. We started seeing intermittent layout shift on large-embedding results (responses > 6k tokens) — odd CSS calc with variable height containers. Repro on Chrome 118 only so far.
  - Small CSS patch deployed to canary (hotfix css-ux-118) reduced shift but not eliminated. Suspect interaction with async streaming element insertion.
  - UX team requests a short-term guard: cap streaming insertion chunk size to avoid heavy reflows.

- Rollout infra (Elena):
  - Canary observability flagged two escalation rules: 1) 95th p50 token-latency spike for panel routes; 2) metrics drop in telemetry for front-end instrumentation (likely related to the layout shift causing dropped events).
  - Rehearsal of fallback policy succeeded in staging. We tested automatic fallback to stable-model-2 when GPU queue > 85% — no rollbacks triggered.
  - Noted a race in the flag evaluation logic: user-session flag sometimes evaluates twice causing duplicate audit entries (INF-3245). We're planning a patch (rollout-fix-dup-flag) today.

- Analytics / Instrumentation (Tom):
  - Missing event: ui.render.complete not firing consistently for streaming responses (affects session-duration sanity checks). Early hypothesis: DOM events fire before the instrumentation hook attaches because of new streaming renderer.
  - Proposed short-term solution: add a lightweight golden-path call at the end of stream lifecycle that emits ui.render.complete if not seen in 2s. Will instrument as feature-flag behind analytics-temp-guard.
  - Need to confirm event semantics with product (Priya) before enabling in prod.

Triage — high-pri tickets called out:
- INF-3245: duplicate flag evaluation -> causes audit spam and occasional 500s on auth path. Impact: small subset of enterprise customers saw errors during big rollout windows.
  - Diagnosis: concurrency issue in flag evaluator when user session state changed during feature-flag read.
  - Decision: emergency patch (rollout-fix-dup-flag) to de-dupe evaluations in the middleware layer.
  - Owner: Elena -> PR by EOD 11/18, testing 11/19 in canary.

- INF-3281: ui.render.complete not emitted for streamed responses leading to undercounted session metrics and mis-triggered rollbacks.
  - Diagnosis: streaming renderer attaches instrumentation hook after initial chunks already started; first chunk causes layout shifts and lost timing window.
  - Decision: implement analytics-temp-guard (emit fallback event) + reduce streaming chunk size to reduce reflow.
  - Owner: Tom -> spike + PR for fallback emitter by 11/19; Marcus to coordinate the chunk-size limiter (UX) and test on canary.

Hotfix plan and verification steps:
- rollout-fix-dup-flag (Elena)
  - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1991 (WIP)
  - Canar y deploy: 11/19 morning; verify metrics (audit events count) and 500 errors reduced.
  - Rollout to prod if no regressions by 11/20 noon.

- css-ux-118 (Marcus) -> temporary CSS + chunk size cap
  - Quick patch in canary, validate with Chrome 118 on multiple viewport sizes.
  - If reflows persist, revert streaming insertion to batch-insert at section boundaries.
  - Verification: manual QA + automated visual-regression on canary by 11/19 EOD.

- analytics-temp-guard (Tom)
  - Feature-flagged emitter; default off for prod. Enable in canary after css patch shows stability.
  - Verification: ui.render.complete event shows in Analytics pipeline for >= 98% of streaming flows for one business hour.

Decisions made:
- Prioritize reliability over micro-latency optimization for streaming renderer today — reduce chunk aggressiveness until visual stability is restored.
- Duplicate flag evaluation hotfix is safe to expedite to canary immediately; team agreed to fast-track.
- Analytics fallback event allowed as temporary safety, but must be gated behind a product review before prod enablement.

Action items (owner -> due):
- Elena -> open/complete PR for INF-3245 patch and smoke test in canary (due 2026-11-19 AM).
- Marcus -> implement streaming chunk cap + extend css fix; run visual-regression checks (due 2026-11-19 EOD).
- Tom -> implement analytics-temp-guard emitter behind flag; add instrumentation test (due 2026-11-19).
- Priya -> coordinate product sign-off for analytics fallback (confirm semantics + rollback criteria) (due 2026-11-19 noon).
- Ravi -> validate staging fallback policy and run synthetic traffic test for fallback triggers (due 2026-11-19).
- Aisha -> notify customer-success of impacted enterprise customers and prepare status note if escalation needed (due 2026-11-19).

Blockers / Unknowns:
- Root cause of Chrome 118-only layout shift still unclear; might be a browser engine timing change interacting with our streaming insertion pattern. Need paired debugging with Chrome devtools and user agent traces.
- Analytics pipeline ingestion delay could mask ui.render.complete counts — need to confirm end-to-end latency on the pipeline for canary events.

Parking lot / follow-ups:
- Long-term: redesign streaming renderer to emit deterministic lifecycle events and support a pluggable instrumentation hook. Scope Q1 2027.
- Investigate adding a front-end QA harness that simulates long streaming responses with large embeds for automated visual checks.

Quick wins / temporary mitigations summary:
- De-dupe flag evaluator (INF-3245) -> fast-track patch
- Cap streaming insertion chunk size -> reduces reflows
- Emit analytics fallback event behind flag -> avoids undercounting session metrics

Next check-in: Monday 2026-11-22 10:00 PT (short follow-up on canary results)

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the visual-regression run limited to the canary pool so we don't flood analytics/metrics.
- If we see more than 3 regression failures in the canary run, revert css-ux-118 and revert streaming changes back to previous stable pattern.
- Add a short postmortem template for the next meeting if issues hit prod (owner for PM + eng).

End of capture.
